ov: A large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot found only in New Zealand, with mottled moss-green feathers and an owl-like face. It is the world's heaviest parrot and the only flightless one. Introduced cats, rats and stoats almost wiped it out; it now lives mostly on predator-free islands.

why.et: Māori once hunted it for its meat and feathers; today every known bird is named, tagged and kept on predator-free islands.

rg: New Zealand only: four small predator-free islands, plus a mainland sanctuary at Maungatautari since 2023.
df: Plants only. It can tell foods apart by smell while foraging at night, which only one other parrot is known to do.

cf.tip: Both are New Zealand parrots, but the kākāpō is a heavy, flightless bird of the ground at night, while the kea flies and lives in South Island forests and mountains.

fx: It may be one of the longest-lived birds, with a reported lifespan of up to 100 years.
It is the only parrot with a lek: males gather and display from bowls they dig in the ground, and females choose between them.
